parsed.prompt_text: What game do you like to play? Say its name and one thing you like about it.
suggested_ideas: Say the name of the game
Say where you play it
Say who you play with
Say one reason you like it

evaluation_guide.expected_content: The speaker names one game and gives one simple detail about liking it.
evaluation_guide.key_points: Name of a game; one clear simple detail such as fun, easy, exciting, or playing with friends.
evaluation_guide.acceptable_responses: The speaker may talk about any familiar game, such as football, badminton, chess, hide-and-seek, or a mobile game. A very short answer is acceptable if it is clear.
evaluation_guide.off_topic_examples: Talking only about a device, explaining game rules in detail, or describing a school subject instead of a game.
evaluation_guide.scoring_hints: Listen for clear pronunciation of common words for games and simple opinion words like fun, good, easy, and like. Short clear answers can score well.
evaluation_guide.common_mistakes: Not naming a game, giving memorized long lists, or speaking too unclearly to identify the game and the reason.

parsed.prompt_text: Look at a game you play now or know well. What simple technology part do you notice, like the screen, sound, or buttons? Say what you can see or hear from it.
suggested_ideas: Name one game you play now or know well
Choose one simple technology part
Say what you can see or hear
Use a short example from that game

evaluation_guide.expected_content: The speaker talks about a game they play now or know well, names one simple technology part, and describes what they can see or hear from it.
evaluation_guide.key_points: A familiar game is mentioned; one simple technology part is named; the answer gives an immediate personal description of what the speaker notices; the response stays simple and relevant.
evaluation_guide.acceptable_responses: Any familiar game is acceptable. The speaker may mention the screen, sound, music, pictures, buttons, or touch controls, and describe what they notice when they play.
evaluation_guide.off_topic_examples: Explaining how game technology works in general, discussing programming or prices, or talking about technology with no clear link to a game the speaker knows.
evaluation_guide.scoring_hints: For PRONUNCIATION, check whether simple words about games and technology are pronounced clearly. Content should be personal, simple, and easy to understand.
evaluation_guide.common_mistakes: Giving a general explanation about games instead of personal information, choosing a technical topic, or pronouncing key words unclearly so the meaning is difficult to follow.

candidates.prompt_text: What game do you like to play or watch? Say its name and describe it in a few simple sentences.
suggested_ideas: Say the name of the game
Say where people play it
Say what players do
Say why it is interesting or fun

evaluation_guide.expected_content: The speaker names one game and gives a short, clear description of it using simple words and short sentences.
evaluation_guide.key_points: One game is clearly identified; at least one or two basic details are given, such as actions, place, rules, or personal opinion; speech is understandable.
evaluation_guide.acceptable_responses: Any common game is acceptable, including digital games, school games, board games, word games, or sports-related games. The speaker may talk about playing it or watching it.
evaluation_guide.off_topic_examples: Talking only about a favorite singer, a school subject, or a holiday without describing any game.
evaluation_guide.scoring_hints: For PRONUNCIATION, focus on whether individual words and short phrases are easy to understand. Minor grammar mistakes are acceptable if pronunciation remains clear.
evaluation_guide.common_mistakes: Not naming a game, giving only one-word answers, speaking too softly, or mispronouncing key words so the game cannot be identified.
